title: San Jose's First Green Stormwater Garden Opens
text:
San Jose has unveiled its first-of-a-kind green infrastructure project, the Riverview Stormwater Garden, a groundbreaking initiative designed to enhance the city’s environmental sustainability efforts. This innovative project showcases how green infrastructure, specifically in the form of a stormwater garden, can improve water quality, manage flood risk, and contribute to a healthier ecosystem. Discover how San Jose is leading the way with this forward-thinking approach to stormwater management .
Riverview Stormwater Garden: A Green Solution for san Jose San jose, Calif. – The city of San Jose marked a significant achievement in its commitment to clean water and environmental sustainability with the inauguration of the Riverview Stormwater Garden. This innovative project promises to enhance water quality and bolster flood control measures.
Project overview Located near Riverview Parkway and Skytop Street,the Riverview Stormwater Garden spans five acres. This bioretention project integrates natural stormwater treatment processes with existing flood management infrastructure. The project has been under advancement for several years.
Key Benefits Enhanced Water Quality: The garden is designed to improve the quality of water discharged into the Guadalupe River. Pollution Reduction: By filtering and treating stormwater, the project aims to reduce pollution levels. Flood Management: The garden will maintain essential flood management functions, protecting the community during heavy rainfall. Long-Term Sustainability: This initiative supports the city’s broader sustainability goals and enhances the resilience of the local stormwater management system. how It Works The Riverview Stormwater Garden repurposes a basin originally constructed over 45 years ago to temporarily store water during heavy rainfall.The updated system now diverts and treats low stormwater flows through filtration and plant uptake before releasing the water into the Guadalupe River.
Related Developments for more information on flood protection efforts in the South Bay,see: Phase 1 of crucial Coyote Creek floodwall almost complete in South Bay, officials say
A Word from the City City officials emphasized the importance of this project during Wednesday morning’s ribbon-cutting ceremony, highlighting its role in supporting long-term sustainability efforts and improving the resilience of the local stormwater management system.
